text:
zoe: heads-up: gryphon-int4 canary for funcall/structured-output shows elevated parse failures but only when streaming + kv_prefix_trim is enabled. posting quick repro and notes.

rahul: how big is elevated? numbers? any templating commonality?

zoe: baseline on fp16/int8 ~0.15% parse_fail. gryphon-int4 at 2.9% on same testset (5k queries). failures cluster on prompts that include an inline markdown table in the system message.

sam: markdown table? interesting. maybe the model produces extra backticks or escapes that break ndjson reassembler. can you paste a raw reassembled stream example?

zoe: pasted below (we reassembled chunks in order exactly as received):

```
system: Note: keep response JSON only
Assistant: processing...
{
  "action": "update_ticket",
  "args": {
    "id": 1234,
    "changes": [
      {"field": "priority", "value": "high"},
      {"field": "owner", "value": "tier-2"}
    ]
  }
}
----META:trace=7f3b

```

zoe: meta footer got injected after the JSON closing brace as a separate chunk. strict parser works here, but other cases are truncated mid-array:

```
[chunk0] "{\n  \"action\": \"update_ticket\",\n  \"args\": {\n    \"changes\": [\n      {\"field\": \"a\", \"value\": \"x\"},\n      {\"field\": \"b\", \"value\": \"y\"},\n"
  "text": "[chunk1] \"    {\\\"field\\\": \\\"c\\\", \\\"value\\\": \\\"z\\\"}\n  ]\n}\n"\n  "text": "[chunk2] \"----META:trace=9c5a\n\n\"\n```

zoe: chunk1 ended without a closing comma or array end because int4 emitted an early EOS token, then chunk2 had the footer. combine==> parse error.

rahul: are these footers generated by our middleware or by model? middleware shouldn't append after stream end but there was a bug where async logging could race. ci-bot: found a recent change: logging-adapter v2.1.3 changed how end-of-stream metrics are flushed (PR #1849).

ci-bot: @rahul flagged PR 1849 in logging-adapter; revert candidate queued.

ivy: even if middleware is racing, why int4 only? hypothesis: quantization shifts tokenization so model emits an explicit '\n' token at different boundary causing stream chunking to split inside the JSON array. combined with our async footer flush, order flips.

sam: we should instrument chunk-level sequence numbers in the reassembler to detect out-of-order or post-EOF footers and drop them. also add a tolerant repair path that will try to close an open array/object and reparse, but only after sanity checks.

zoe: quick mitigation I tried: discard any chunk starting with /^----META:/ if it arrives after what looks like a closed JSON (we detect a trailing '}' + optional whitespace). that brought canary parse_fail to 0.6%.

rahul: sounds like a pragmatic short fix. longer term: two tracks: A) revert logging-adapter change and fix async flush ordering (infra), B) harden reassembler + add chunk-seq-number (runtime).

sam: addendum: for the repair path we should compute a similarity score of repaired JSON vs model's last successful non-repaired output on the same prompt (semantic hash) to avoid silently changing intent. record repaired=true in eval telemetry.

ivy: also add a test in the onboarding harness: run edge-case prompts (long tables, multi-line code blocks, NDJSON arrays) against quantized variants with streaming enabled and assert parse_fail < 0.5% or repairs <= 0.5% separately.

zoe: created infra ticket LOG-902 to revert/fix adapter and runtime ticket RUNTIME-442 for chunk-seq and tolerant-repair. added test case to onboarding (EVAL-1207).

rahul: timeline? can we patch canary tonight with the chunk-drop rule and start 48h run?

zoe: yes I'll push sanitizer rule to canary at 01:00 UTC, enable chunk-seq debug logging, and share metrics snapshot after 12h.

sam: thanks. low priority note: check if customers using private deployments will need SDK change — if sanitizer becomes default it should be opt-out.

zoe: agreed. making SDK opt-out flag and default on for hosted.

rahul: nice work. keep tickets linked in this thread and close when canary meets targets.

zoe: linking LOG-902, RUNTIME-442, EVAL-1207 in thread. end.
